reason: I'd probably try the free framework part, but the paid stuff (interview guide, methodology, transcript coding) is exactly what I already do with ChatGPT Plus and my supervisor, so another $49 on top of my subscription is hard to justify on my stipend. The 'never writes your text' line is reassuring, but it doesn't change what I'd pay for.
objection: I don't know if my department would see uploading interview transcripts to an AI tool as misuse, or as an ethics problem with participant data, and there's nothing here saying any university or supervisor has signed off on it.
would_change_my_mind: My supervisor or graduate school saying it's fine to use, plus a clear statement on how transcript data is stored, would make me pay for it when I get to the analysis stage.
